operant-conditioning-s3.title: Placeholder: schedules and persistence in rats

study.introduction: Placeholder: researchers asked whether the schedule of reinforcement changes how long rats keep pressing a lever.
study.participants: Placeholder: 40 laboratory rats, randomly assigned to one of four schedules. An animal care committee approved the study.
study.method: Placeholder: each rat pressed a lever for food on its schedule for two weeks; then food stopped and presses were counted for 30 minutes.
study.results: Placeholder: rats on the variable-ratio schedule pressed most after food stopped.

items.q: Placeholder: a teen's curfew is extended after a week of finished chores, and chores get done more often. Which concept explains the change?

why.correct: Placeholder: something pleasant was added and the behavior increased.
options: Right: a pleasant consequence was added.
Removing a privilege lowers a behavior.
Adding something unpleasant lowers a behavior.

items.q: Placeholder: a pigeon was reinforced after 3, 5, 7 and 5 pecks. What is the mean number of pecks per reinforcement?

mistakes.why: Placeholder: 20 is the total. Divide by the number of values, 4.

items.q: Placeholder: a seatbelt alarm stops when a driver buckles up, and drivers buckle up faster. Which concept is this?

why.correct: Placeholder: an unpleasant sound is removed and the behavior increases.
options: Removing something pleasant lowers a behavior.

items.q: Placeholder: five rats pressed a lever 2, 4, 4, 9 and 16 times. What is the median?

why.correct: Placeholder: in order, the middle value is 4.

mistakes.why: Placeholder: 7 is the mean. The median is the middle score in order.

items.q: Placeholder: what is the range of the response counts in the table?

items.q: Placeholder: by the 68-95-99.7 rule, what percent of scores lie between 85 and 115 on this curve?

why.correct: Placeholder: one standard deviation each side of the mean holds 68%.

mistakes.why: Placeholder: 34% is one side only. Add both sides.

items.q: Placeholder: a score of 130 on this curve is about which percentile?

why.correct: Placeholder: two standard deviations above the mean is about the 98th percentile.
options: That is one standard deviation above.
68% is a share between two marks, not a percentile.
